title: Kingdom of Dunoting
capsule: Dunoding (also rendered Dunoting) was an early medieval sub-kingdom within the broader realm of Gwynedd in northwest Wales, occupying the coastal lowlands and hills of what is now the Llŷn Peninsula and Eifionydd district. It took its name from Dunod, a son of Cunedda Wledig, the fifth-century king credited with expelling Irish settlers from northwestern Britain, and its ruling line is known primarily from later medieval Welsh genealogical sources. The attestation window 592–626 falls in the period when Gwynedd's sub-kingdoms were consolidating under Cadfan ap Iago and his successors, and Dunoding's rulers at this point are unattested by contemporary documents. The kingdom eventually dissolved, probably by the tenth century, its territory divided between the cantrefi of Eifionydd and Ardudwy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Dunoding is attested only through post-Norman Welsh genealogical sources compiled centuries after the period in question; the territorial extent and even the existence of distinct governance in the 592–626 window are speculative, and confidence in any mapped boundary is very low.
